question.prompt: In year \(N,\) the \(300\)th day of the year is a Tuesday. In year \(N + 1,\) the \(200\)th day is also a Tuesday. On what day of the week did the \(100\)th day of year \(N - 1\) occur?

solutions.explanation:
Two dates have the same weekday exactly when the number of days between them is a multiple of \(7\). Let \(L\) be the number of days in year \(N\). From its \(300\)th day to the \(200\)th day of the next year, the elapsed time is
\[
(L-300)+200=L-100.
\]
For an ordinary year this would be \(265=7\cdot37+6\) days, which cannot connect two Tuesdays. For a leap year it is \(266=7\cdot38\) days. Thus year \(N\) is a leap year.

Leap years are not consecutive, so year \(N-1\) has \(365\) days. From its \(100\)th day to the \(300\)th day of year \(N\), the elapsed time is
\[
(365-100)+300=565=7\cdot80+5.
\]
The desired day is therefore five weekdays before Tuesday. Counting backward gives Monday, Sunday, Saturday, Friday, Thursday. Hence the answer is \(\boxed{\text{Thursday}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
solutions.title: Count elapsed days and complete weeks
